prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Make ONE coherent right-facing WALK animation from the attached exact player sprite reference. The reference character design is immutable: SAME head silhouette, black hair tufts, ONE visible eye in right side profile, face shape, warm skin tone, muted dark olive shirt, yellow neck scarf, cream sleeve cuffs, brown belt trousers and boots. Same head/body size ratio as reference. Retain small-game sprite rendering and outline weight; no character redesign, no added details, no thicker body, no larger head.
Output transparent sprite sheet EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and TWO ROWS, eight chronological frames read left-to-right top row then left-to-right bottom row. All eight figures face exactly RIGHT in the SAME side profile as reference. Exact same head/face artwork in all cells, translated vertically at most a tiny amount. Same overall scale, torso thickness and limb segment lengths in all eight. Same light, skin and clothes colors throughout. Generous empty transparent cell margins. Full hair and feet visible, no labels, no grid, no shadow, no other characters.

CRITICAL CHANGE: arms swing FORWARD AND BACK FROM THE SHOULDERS, hands DOWN near the hips, elbows only slightly bent; NOT fists stuck together at chest or waist, not carrying, not running. Boots roll heel-to-toe and legs alternate, never shuffle in one repeated pose. Near arm and far arm swing in opposite directions and opposite to their respective legs. Near limbs have same light as reference; far limbs slightly occluded/darker only as appropriate. Keep both arms anatomically attached to shoulders, knees and ankles connected naturally.

Frame1 NEAR leg extended forward to RIGHT, heel touching ground, toe raised; FAR leg extended back to LEFT, toe on ground. NEAR arm swings BACK/LEFT, FAR arm FORWARD/RIGHT.
Frame2 near foot settles flat and supports weight, far heel lifts; near arm starts returning toward hip.
Frame3 near leg vertical supporting weight, far leg bends and passes forward under hip; arms pass close to hips on opposite sides.
Frame4 near foot pushes off its toe BEHIND to LEFT, far leg extends forward RIGHT about to contact; NEAR arm swings FORWARD RIGHT, FAR arm BACK LEFT.
Frame5 FAR leg heel contacts forward RIGHT, NEAR leg trailing LEFT toe touches ground. NEAR arm FORWARD RIGHT, FAR arm BACK LEFT. This is OPPOSITE leg/arm assignment to frame1.
Frame6 far foot settles flat supporting weight, near heel lifts; near arm returns toward hip.
Frame7 far leg vertical supports weight, near leg bends and passes forward under hip; arms pass hips, opposite of frame3.
Frame8 far foot pushes off toe behind LEFT, near leg extends forward RIGHT to return seamlessly into frame1. Near arm swings BACK LEFT, far arm FORWARD RIGHT.

A relaxed WALK with at least one foot grounded throughout. No flight phase. Clear distinct contact, down, passing, up positions. Body stays upright. Foot ground line identical in every cell. This is a production animation test, not eight independent illustrations. Do not repeat the same leading leg across both half cycles.
